label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKE AFTERMATH.

label: text
text:
Anti-British Agitation
Continues.

label: text
text: EX-PICKETS ON THE BUND.

label: text
text: Passengers' Argument Leads to Badly Injured Head.

label: text
text: Anticipations recorded in the "China Mail" yesterday have been borne out, with regard to agitation in Canton against patronage of so-called British-owned ships, as different from Chinese-owned vessels under British registry.

label: text
text: Assumed to be ex-pickets, unarmed men in plain-clothes have posted themselves on the West Bund, near the Hong Kong boats' wharves, and are actively searching passengers' effects and 'examining' cargo.

label: text
text: Other men are haranguing intending passengers to refrain from going on the Steamboat Co's steamers but to travel instead by the ships owned by Chinese. There has been no intimidation but the "warnings" delivered in the manner described have had an effect.

label: text
text:
Outside Companies' Benefit.
The result is that the "outside" steamboats on the Hong Kong-Canton run are getting more passengers and cargo, comparatively.

label: text
text: The quota of passengers still remains very high. Ex-strikers accepting the gratuity of $10 to depart for work still form a considerable portion of the number of passengers.

label: text
text: Because it is possible to work at night in Hong Kong, the Tung On Co. is bringing down more cargo than up to Canton. as the time after arrival there each day is only a few hours before dark. Even then this line is not shipping any piccegoods to Canton.

label: text
text: To aggravate the piecegoods position, trouble has again broken out—so it is reported—among the dealers' and shop's employees in Canton city.

label: text
text:
Varying Conditions,
In spite of the fact that British cargo on the s.s. "Tai Ming" was not landed at Wuchow, some of the boats on that run are still carrying cargo upwards, including British manufactures.

label: text
text: To Kongmoon, the trade is still below normal figures but early improvement is confidently expected.

label: text
text: In Swätow, native employees have ignored the agitation and the shortage of domestic servants is over. Trade has yet to improve but conditions are not disencouraging.

label: text
text: An incident near, the Bund yesterday morning may be misconstrued by rumour mongers. Two friends were walking together to embark on a Hong Kong boat when they quarrelled as to which of the three leaving at 8 a.m. should be taken. They ultimately came to blows and one had his head badly injured. Beyond cheering on the combatants the Strikers' searchers in the vicinity took no part.

label: text
text: Another sign of improvement is the shipment to North China ports, by British steamers, of Canton cargo via Hong Kong. Such merchandise is brought to the companies' wharves and/or godowns in Canton and put on the ship there. The placing of transport facilities, by the shipping agents, at the Chinese merchants' disposal, has helped materially to overcome difficulties.

label: text
text: Further inquiries by the "China Mail" point to an outlook that has much promise.

label: text
text: Although seemingly reluctant to curb the activities of the pickets who have now organised themselves as searchers, the Canton authorities are considered by the merchants in Canton as favourable to speedy resumption.

label: text
text: Owing to the time necessary for the machinery to be set in operation, the Surtax Bureau is not working at full pitch in Canton, much less in outports.

label: text
text:
As mentioned in yesterday's "China Mail," the Canton Government expects about $250,000 a month in the special taxes on exports from Canton alone. It has not been possible to frame an estimate for outports and upcountry stations but the work is proceeding.
Trade will have resumed pre-strike proportions by China Now

text: SURREYS

label: paragraph_title
text: CROWDS WITNESS FAREWELL

label: text
text: DEPARTURE FOR INDIA.

label: text
text: Preceded by the pipes and brass bands of the King's Own Scottish Bonderers and with the Regimental Colours in the middle of the column, the 1st East Surveys Battillon with full kit, marched in column of route this morning through the principal thoroughfare of the city.

label: text
text: The route from the Barracks lay by way of Des' Vaux Road, the Post Office, Star Ferry, and Cenotort, to the Prince of Wales gate of the Naval Yard through which the Battalion passed prior to disembarkation on the s.s. "Neuralia" which is to take them to India.

label: text
text: The progress of the March, which was very effective by reason of the martial music, glittering array of bayqjets, the length of the column, and the precision of the movement was witnessed by large crowds.

label: text
text: The Scottish bands accompanied the march as far as the ferry and the East Surveys Bapd, stationed outside the Hong Kong Hotel, struck up the "Regimental" March ("A Southerly Wind and a Quiet Sky") as the troops marched past the Geohatch where the General Officer Commanding (Major General C. C. Luard) took the salute.

label: text
text: The "Neurulia" left shortly after 1 p.m."

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: NORTHERN SUCCESS

label: paragraph_title
text: Fighting over "Classical"

label: text
text: ABOUT CHANG KAI-SHEK.

label: text
text: Cantonese Counter-Attacked on

label: text
text: Successes are claimed for the Northern Allies, in their counter-attacks on three fronts, against the Cantonese Expedition.

label: text
text: General Yang Sen, of Wanhien notoriety, is pushing eastwards towards Hunan province and attacking the west of the Nationalist new territory.

label: text
text: In his march, he has covered several places in the "battlefield of China," of the classical days of the "Three Kingdoms"—several centuries B.C.

label: text
text: At that time the greatest War Minister China has ever had (Chu Ruo-liang) made the fatal mistake of venturing from the mountains of Szechuan" (it was Sal-chuén in those days) to attack rival kingdoms of the middle Yangtse Valley. Yang Sen, however, has the advantage in that his enemy is also fighting on the east.

label: text
text: Simultaneously, other Northern detachments are moving on Hupeh and Hunan provinces, these being the so-called subordinates of Marshall Wu Pei-fu, who are demonstrating southwards from Shinyang and Wu-sheng-kwan Pass.

label: text
text: But it is on the lower Yangtse (on the Kiangsi front) that the most severe action of the week has been fought.

label: text
text: From his main camp at Kiukiang and his naval base at Wusueh (both on the Yangtse), Marshal Sun Chuan-fang has sent his army eastwards to push back the left flank of the Cantonese.

label: text
text: A few weeks ago, Sun's men rave up several advanced points they had taken and they are now following the old route in their endeavour to reach Wuchang and Hankow.

label: text
text: With regard to yesterday's Reuter cable about General Chang Kai-shek's wound it should be noted that one message was from Kiukiang. The doctor who arrived there—and it is a pity that neither his name nor nationality were given—was in Sun Chuan-fang's headquarters.

label: text
text:
The other message about Chang being an inmate at the Changsha hospital and that his leg was to be amputated, is an official report from Sun's headquarters (presumably also in Kiukiang).
A section of the local vernacular Press still maintains that Canton's soldier of the hour is either dead or seriously wounded. They point to the Kuomintang resolution asking Mr. Wong Ching-wai (Political chairman) to return to office, as meeting the necessity of appointing a new leader; and further capital is made out of the resolution by alleging—with what amount of truth is unknown—that Chang Kalshek exerted pressure to get Mr. Wong out of the way and that the invitation would not have been extended unless Chang's influence had disappeared!

label: paragraph_title
text:
Chang Wounded Report.
Kiukianó. Oct. 21

label: text
text: General Yueh, Commander of the 1st Allied Division, said:—“As the main body of the Southern troops under the direct command of General Chang Kai-shek closed in upon... Nanchang, our troops closed the gates on Oct. 11 and defended the city. At 4 o'clock on Oct. 13, we formed a dare-to-die corps and sent them out in three directions. They made surprise attacks on the headquarters of General Lu Ting-ping as well as of General Chang Kai-shek, in spite of the enemy's sentinels and advance posts. The attacks were quite effective, beyond our expectations, and the enemy began to beat a retreat in a disorderly manner.”

label: text
text: General Chang Kai-shek was wounded in this battle. At the same time one of the three Russian attaches at General Chang's headquarters was also wounded. It appears that General Chang is now concentrating his routed soldiers at Changshu—“Toho”.

text: LOCAL WEDDING.

label: text
text: CEREMONY AT ST. ANDREWS, KOWLOON

label: text
text: PINGUET—WITCHELL.

label: text
text: St. Andrew's Church, Kowloon, was the scene of a pretty wedding this afternoon, the parties being Miss M. D. Mitchell, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. R. C. Mitchell, of Hong Kong; and Mr. Ernest Lewis Pinguet, also of Hong Kong.

label: text
text: The Rev. G. R. Lindsay officiated, assisted by the Rev. G. E. Arrowsmith, Mr. R. Baldwin was at the organ.

label: text
text:
The bride, who was given away by her father, was attired in white broaded silk and georgette with embroidered veil and orange blossoms. Her bouquet was of white reses and maiden hair fern.
Miss Eveline Pinguet, sister of the bridegroom, was bridesmaid and Miss Dorothy Mitchell, sister of the bride, was flower girl. The former wore a dress of pink crepe de chine with heavily beaded panels and pink picture hat and carried a bouquet of pink roses and cosmos, whilst the latter was attired in a dress of floral georgette over lemon crepe-de-chine with white shoes and socks and wreath of silver and water lilies.

label: text
text: The bride's mother wore a dress of black georgette and velvet and black hat.

label: text
text: outside the city were laid waste by fire in the course of battles, while a large number of houses inside were also destroyed. Taking advantage of the chaotic conditions, looting started, and many rich men and merchants were heavily affected, having sustained loss to a considerable amount. All the houses were closed, followed by the suspension of business and banking transactions. When General Cheng Chun-yen (Northern Allies) entered the city the streets were derked with the Chinese national flags.—“Shanghai Mercury.”

label: paragraph_title
text: ON NANCHOW FRONT.

label: paragraph_title
text: Wu Pei-fu & Yang Sen Both Advance.

label: text
text: General Yang Sen's troops, on Oct. 19, captured "Nanhsien on the northern shores of Lake Dungting and are now marching on Yochow. The Southerners station at Kung-an in Hupeh province, are also reported to have been defeated by General Yang Sen's forces, with the consequence that the Southern troops at Changteh have become shaky. On the other hand, Marshal Wu Pei-fu's forces are at present advancing from the border of Honan into Hupeh, where the situation is greatly strained. There is little or no change in conditions on all battle lines in Kiangsi.—"Toho."

label: paragraph_title
text: GUNS IN MISSION.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chang Kai-shek in Charge at Nanchang.

label: text
text: The first Red Cross party, which left Kuling some three weeks ago have returned safely.

label: text
text: They report that severe nighting took place at Nanchang last week — continuous fighting from Oct. 14 to 17.

label: text
text: Hand to hand fighting took place; the walls were scaled by Southerners and the latter entered one of the gates, but later left by another gate.

label: text
text: The Southerners finally withdrew to a position, south of Nanchang, about 9 miles away, and are entrenched there, waiting for further supplies and ammunition. There have been severe losses on both sides.

label: text
text: The Southerners actually placed some of their guns in the compound of the Methodist Episcopal Mission, thus drawing the firing of the Northerners on to that compound.

label: text
text:
Southerners Will Return.
Despite strong objections which were raised by the senior members of that Mission, Chang Kalshek who was personally in charge of the fighting, refused to have the guns moved away.
Another large gun was also placed on property belonging to the American Mission, but we understand was removed later.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL CONFERENCE

label: paragraph_title
text: Trades Unionists See Prime Minister.

label: text
text: Tri-Party Meeting Urged on the Government.

label: text
text: London Oct.: 23.

label: text
text: The Prime Minister, accompanied by the Chancellor of the Exchequer and the Minister for Mines, met representatives of the Trades Union Congress in the Prime Minister's Room in the House of Commons this evening at the latter's request and discussed the coal situation.

label: text
text: The proceedings were secret, but it is believed that the Trade Unions Congress requested the summoning of the coal owners' and miners' representatives.

label: text
text:
The Prime Minister replied that Government intervention was useless whilst the present attitude of the two sides persisted.
Nevertheless the Trade Union Congress does not regard the interview as abortive, and has some hope of further meetings.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Appeal To Miners.

label: paragraph_title
text: Rugby, October 26.

label: text
text:
Colonel Lane Fox, the Secretary for Mines, speaking late in last night's Commons' coal debate, made an earnest appeal for provincial district settlements, expressing the view that if such a course were sanctioned by the Miners' Federation, there could be an agreement within a week in the majority of districts. He particularly emphasised that such a step would not destroy the Federation but would leave it in exactly the same position as it held up to 1921.
The industry existed under district settlements till that date, and if the Federation had the confidence of the men it represented, they would remain. It was evident that under present conditions there were some districts which at any rate for a time would require some extension of hours if they were to maintain a decent and reasonable rate of wages. He said the Government would not risk further robuffs until there was evidence of good sense as well as good will on the part of the disputants.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: 7,000.More Mến Resume.

label: text
text: Over 250,000 miners are now working, the official figures being 253,000. There was an increase of 7,000 to-day.—Reuten.

label: text
text: Defending in the House of Commons the renewal of the Emergency Regulations Sir William Joynson-Hicks, Home Secretary, said that the number of cases dealt with under the Regulations during the past month had shown a decrease. During the past month he had felt some anxiety as to the sufficiency of the Police force in certain parts of the country, having "regard" to the potentialities of trouble. There had, however, been not many but only a few sporadic cases of disorder.

label: text
text: He had communicated with the Chief Constable in the district's whilst the coal stoppage existed asking them whether they had sufficient Police and whether they wanted support. Most of the Chief Constable gave a satisfactory report on the condition of affairs, and reinforcements of police had been sent to only three or four places.

label: paragraph_title
text: Peaceful Picketing

label: text
text:
The right of peaceful picketing was still allowed, and he appealed to members having influence in the mining areas to see that it was not abused. So far, he gladly admitted that the dispute had been conducted without grave disorder, and this said a great deal for the good temper of the mining community and of the Police in their difficult duty.
The chief virtue of the Regulations was that under them offences could be dealt with more quickly than if they were remitted to Assize Courts. Possible sentences at Assizes were, moreover, four times as heavy.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text:
London, Oct. 26.
The House of Commons adopted by 185 votes to 68 the continuance for a month of the Emergency Regulations, and then adjourned till November 9.—Reuter.
